name: Prakriti - the Ideation
quote: In all things of nature there is something of the marvelous.
paragraphs: To me, nature represents more than the world around us. It is a living source of imagination, innovation, and discovery. It reminds us that some of the most powerful ideas begin quietly as observations, questions, or unfinished experiments.
This series is the space for those beginnings: original thoughts, ideation, and fresh perspectives that are still taking shape.

name: Sāṅkhya - the Exploration
quote: If you can't explain it simply, you don't understand it well enough.
paragraphs: Sāṅkhya comes from the Sanskrit for enumeration and analysis - the discipline of understanding something by taking it apart, piece by piece, down to its roots. It names knowledge that is earned through depth rather than skimmed from the surface.

This is where things slow down and go deep. These posts unpack the fundamentals - the concepts most of us use without ever examining - and take them back to first principles, explained properly. Expect careful breakdowns, the why beneath the what, and the patient work of making a hard idea genuinely clear. Where Prakriti asks new questions, Sankhya answers old ones thoroughly. It's for anyone who would rather understand a thing completely than merely recognize it.

name: Nazarya - the Outcome
quote: A line is a dot that went for a walk.
paragraphs: 'Nazarya' translates to a perspective, or a way of seeing.

When it comes to learning, how we view a concept changes how we understand it. This series defines a specific lens for that journey—one focused entirely on practical application rather than pure theory.
It is a space for tangible artifacts: illustrations of complex thoughts, structured preparation materials, and the final results of the ideation process.
